land.text: six of the seven Trucial sheikhdoms (Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah) united on 2 December 1971

successors.note: Ras Al Khaimah, the seventh, 'joined on 10 February 1972'. Cliopatria's United Arab Emirates row starts only in 1973; the Trucial States' last three years are therefore drawn from this dossier's own 1895 keyframe.

capitals.name: Abu Dhabi
capitals.note: The infobox names Abu Dhabi; the same page calls the government a 'tribal confederation(s)' and gives no capitals for the sheikhdoms, so Abu Dhabi stands for the confederation's most senior seat.

keyframe_review.note: 73,358 km2 for 1820-1852: a footprint of the modern United Arab Emirates (93% of its cells, plus 27 cells of Oman and Saudi Arabia on the edge). The page gives no area; it names the members Abu Dhabi, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah (1820), Dubai (1833) and, later, Kalba and Fujairah. The shape stands as the confederation's land.

correction.text: unchanged outline through the Perpetual Maritime Truce of 4 May 1853

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1853-1855, a gap in Cliopatria's Name: the infobox gives the Perpetual Maritime Truce of 4 May 1853, so the confederation does not lapse; the 1820 outline holds.
72,350 km2 for 1856-1869: the same footprint within 2%; the page records no border change.

71,807 km2 for 1870-1872: the same footprint (a few fringe cells fewer); no border change on the page. The Faisal page has Faisal attacking the Trucial States in the 1860s until 'the British forces militarily stopped his attacks', so the Saudi neighbour never held ground (the Nejd shape of 1856 reached the coast only by Cliopatria's drawing).
73,472 km2 for 1873-1889: the same footprint again; no border change on the page.
73,472 km2 for 1890-1894: the 1873 outline. The Exclusive Agreement of 6-8 March 1892 put the six rulers 'under British protection' and kept the borders ('not to cede territory except to Britain').

correction.text: the 1890 outline held to 1971, less the Tunbs and Abu Musa from November 1971

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1895-1971, a gap in Cliopatria's Name (its last shape ends in 1894): the page dates the state to 1971 and describes no change of land until the loss of the Tunbs and Abu Musa in November 1971. Kalba had trucial status 1936-1951 and was reincorporated into Sharjah, and Fujairah joined in 1952, both inside the footprint. The Buraimi oasis division with Oman (Buraimi and Hamasa to Oman, Al Ain to Abu Dhabi) is undated on the page and not drawn.

region.text: the sheikhdoms of the coast that adhered to the treaty

ledger.note: 8 January 1820: the sheikhs of the coast sign the General Maritime Treaty with Britain. Page: infobox 'General Maritime Treaty: 8 January 1820'; 'A peace treaty was signed in 1820 to which all the sheikhs of the coast adhered' (Abu Dhabi, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Sharjah and Umm Al Quwain; Dubai from 1833).

region.text: the Trucial Coast under British protection

ledger.note: 6-8 March 1892: the Exclusive Agreement puts the rulers under British protection. Page: signed by the rulers of Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah and Umm Al Quwain; 'the British promised to protect the Trucial Coast from all aggression by sea and to help in case of land attack' and the sheikhs agreed 'not to dispose of any territory except to Britain'. The Persian Gulf Residency status runs from 1820 (infobox) but the protection is dated 1892.

region.text: the Buraimi oasis, contested (Saudi guards in Hamasa)

ledger.note: 31 August 1952: Saudi guards occupy Hamasa. Page: 'On 31 August 1952, a group of some 80 Saudi Arabian guards, 40 of whom were armed,' crossed Abu Dhabi territory and occupied Hamasa, led by the Emir of Ras Tanura; Saudi claims rested on Wahhabi influence over the oasis 'in the period between 1800-1869'. Reviewer me-10-f (2026-10-25): occupation pair changed to a contest pair: the page calls Hamasa 'one of three Omani villages in the oasis', so the Saudi occupation was of Omani land (kingdom-of-saudi-arabia /ledger/8-9 record it against sultanate-of-oman); for the Trucial States the oasis was contested, mirroring kingdom-of-saudi-arabia /ledger/7.

region.text: the Buraimi oasis, contested (Saudi guards in Hamasa)

ledger.note: 25 October 1955: the Trucial Oman Levies retake Buraimi. Page: Britain 'decided to unilaterally abrogate the Standstill Agreement and take the oasis on 25 October 1955'; the Levies 'quickly took the oasis and captured the Saudi contingent'. Later division (undated): Oman got Buraimi and Hamasah, Abu Dhabi the village of Al Ain and its oases; settled by the Treaty of Jeddah of 1974. Reviewer me-10-f (2026-10-25): occupation pair changed to a contest pair: the page calls Hamasa 'one of three Omani villages in the oasis', so the Saudi occupation was of Omani land (kingdom-of-saudi-arabia /ledger/8-9 record it against sultanate-of-oman); for the Trucial States the oasis was contested, mirroring kingdom-of-saudi-arabia /ledger/10.

region.text: Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunbs (not in the gazetteer)

ledger.note: 29-30 November 1971: Iran seizes the Tunbs and Abu Musa. Page: infobox 'Iran seized Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunbs 29-30 November 1971'; the text says the islands were taken from Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah's claim to Abu Musa. The Abu Musa page: on 30 November Sharjah and Iran signed a memorandum letting Iranian troops land while Sharjah kept a police station; the Tunbs were taken two days earlier. The memorandum leaves Abu Musa shared.
1 December 1971: British protection ends. Page: 'the treaties were revoked on 1 December 1971'.

region.text: the six sheikhdoms of the union and Ras Al Khaimah to follow

ledger.note: 2 December 1971: six Trucial States form the United Arab Emirates. Page: the protectorate ended on 1 December 1971; 'formed the United Arab Emirates' on 2 December, with Ras Al Khaimah joining on 10 February 1972.

wars.name: Faisal's attacks on the Trucial States
wars.outcome: Faisal bin Turki 'attacked' the Trucial States in the 1860s and 'the British forces militarily stopped his attacks'; no land changed hands.
wars.note: The page gives only 'the 1860s'; the years here are the decade.

wars.name: Buraimi Dispute
wars.outcome: Saudi guards occupied Hamasa on 31 August 1952; a Standstill Agreement (30 July 1954) and arbitration at Geneva (1955) failed; the Trucial Oman Levies retook the oasis on 25 October 1955. The dispute was settled in 1974 by the Treaty of Jeddah.
wars.note: Oman's sultan and the imam both mobilised in 1952 and stood down.

wars.name: Iranian occupation of Abu Musa and the Tunbs

zones.text: Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunbs (not in the gazetteer)

wars.outcome: Iran took the Tunbs by force and Abu Musa by a memorandum with Sharjah on 30 November 1971, two days before the UAE was proclaimed.
wars.note: Earlier Iranian moves (1904 flag, 1923, twenty days in 1964) took no land.

certainty.note: The 1820 and 1853 truces fix no boundaries; the sheikhdoms' limits are tribal and the inland frontier with Najd and Oman is undefined.
The Exclusive Agreement of 1892 fixes protection, not frontiers; the Buraimi frontier was settled only in 1974 (Treaty of Jeddah) and the island frontier with Iran never.

sources.title: Trucial States
sources.note: Dates and members (1820-1971), the 1820, 1853 and 1892 agreements, the end on 1 and 2 December 1971, Kalba 1936-1951, Fujairah 1952, Iran's seizure of the islands. The infobox gave no area and a blank 'preceded by'.

sources.title: Buraimi Dispute
sources.note: Saudi occupation of Hamasa on 31 August 1952, the 1954-1955 arbitration, the retaking on 25 October 1955, the later division and the 1974 settlement.

sources.title: Abu Musa
sources.note: Sharjah's control of Abu Musa, the 1904, 1923 and 1964 Iranian moves, the memorandum and landing of 30 November 1971.

sources.title: Faisal bin Turki bin Abdullah Al Saud
sources.note: Faisal's attacks on the Trucial States in the 1860s, stopped by British forces (also cited in emirate-of-nejd).

notes:
Cliopatria's Name 'Trucial States' ends in 1894 and has a gap in 1853-1855; the page dates the state 1820-1971, so the dossier runs to 1 December 1971 and adds new keyframes for 1853-1855 and 1895-1971 (the same United Arab Emirates footprint, since no page describes a border change before November 1971). Cliopatria's United Arab Emirates row starts in 1973, so 1971-1972 has no other source of shape.

Budget: the page budget was 5; four pages were opened (Trucial States, Buraimi Dispute, Abu Musa and, shared with emirate-of-nejd, the Faisal page). The Trucial States infobox has no area; no infobox comparison was possible. The five shapes of 1820-1894 differ by under 2%, which no page explains and which looks like Cliopatria's neighbour clipping, not history.

Unsettled: (1) the division of the Buraimi oasis (Buraimi and Hamasa to Oman, Al Ain to Abu Dhabi) is undated on the page, so there is no event; Cliopatria's footprint carries 25% of the Buraymi governorate of Oman; (2) the Tunbs, taken from Ras Al Khaimah, and Abu Musa (Sharjah) are each smaller than one resolution-5 grid cell (about 250 km2), so their regions resolve to no cells and the renderer should treat the November 1971 events as captions only; they are written as 15 km discs; (3) Ras Al Khaimah joined the UAE on 10 February 1972, after this state's end; (4) the sheikhdoms (Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Fujairah, Kalba) have no dossiers of their own; the page gives their dates but not their borders, and a gap-filler could open the Emirate articles; (5) the counterpart 'united-kingdom' is the slug eu-11's split of Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Great Britain' should create.

Region names the gazetteer lacks: Abu Musa (25.87 N, 55.03 E), Greater Tunb (26.26 N, 55.31 E) and Lesser Tunb (26.24 N, 55.14 E), used as 15 km discs.
